meta.name: explainer-knowledge-graph
meta.purpose: Machine-readable rules + parameters + patterns for generating SaaS explainer videos. Consumed by Editron 'Explainer Mode' (LLM scene-planner emits a SceneGraph; the generative composer + renderer turn it into a recipe of primitives). The LLM never writes render code (Rule 30); this graph bounds what it plans and how the engine composes.
meta.consumer_status: NOT yet wired — canonical source artifact. When Explainer Mode is built, copy to lib/editron/data/explainer-knowledge-graph.json.

evidence_legend.E: Established — peer-reviewed or near-universal craft law. Trust.
evidence_legend.I: Industry data/heuristic — credible first-party/practitioner data. Default; A/B if it matters.
evidence_legend.T: Tunable default — starting value to CALIBRATE on real renders + watch-through (Rule 31). Never ship as fact.
evidence_legend.M: Marketing-claim — single secondary source, directional only.

meta.calibration_note: Every node with confidence 'T' is a starting default, not a fact. Calibrate against real Editron renders and watch-through data per Rule 31.

laws.statement: ONE message per video; two selling points dilute both.
Win the hook in <=3s with a felt problem, an outcome/aha (open loop), or a pattern interrupt; never open with self-introduction.
VO words <= 2.2 x seconds; talk fills <=85% of runtime, leaving silence for visuals/aha.
Spine = ordered scene ROLES (hook -> stakes -> solution -> capability beats -> proof -> cta), not fixed templates.
Benefit-led and specific; raise desire and remove confusion (Purchase = Desire - Labor - Confusion).
No triple redundancy (narration + identical on-screen text + redundant graphic); cut extraneous cognitive load.
Dwell long enough to read comprehension beats; keep mechanical motion fast; cut to music BPM; insert breathers.
Front-load value; open a curiosity loop early and close it at the payoff.
Captions always (sound-off default); narrate complex visuals; let aha beats breathe in silence.
Motion congruent with meaning; ease + stagger + anticipation; choreography computed from tokens, never hardcoded frames.
Brand hue sovereign; semantic colors fixed (green/red/amber/blue); mood via saturation+brightness+temperature; WCAG contrast floors are hard.
Use match cuts (carry one meaningful element across the cut) and premium product-UI camera (zoom/track/click) for the expensive feel.
Music builds to the payoff and resolves at the end (real outro); SFX punctuate sparingly and varied (overuse = fatigue).
One visual voice per video + 3 signature easing curves (motion equity); generate form from tokens, never select a template.
Length and aspect are a function of format x platform; end on exactly ONE call to action.

frameworks.name: Hook-Problem-Solution-CTA
frameworks.note: Universal backbone; PAS/AIDA/BAB/StoryBrand all rearrange this.

frameworks.name: Attention-Interest-Desire-Action
frameworks.use_case: buildup; launches, landing pages, cold audiences

frameworks.name: StoryBrand SB7
frameworks.use_case: homepage/hero; customer=hero, product=guide with a plan + CTA, avoiding failure -> success
frameworks.rule: Never make the product the hero.

scene_roles.purpose: Stop the scroll; state the felt problem or show the outcome (open loop).
Agitate the problem / show the painful status quo.
Introduce the product as the inevitable answer (meet the guide).
One benefit, shown not told (UI/demo). Repeat 2-4x.
Optional silence/space beat between dense sections.

scene_graph_schema.description: The structured output the LLM scene-planner emits (DATA, not code). The generative composer turns each scene into a recipe of primitives bounded by this graph's laws/params.

scenes.copy: string (on-screen headline/phrase — short, never the VO verbatim)
scenes.vo_line: string (narration for this scene; obey words<=2.2*duration)
scenes.ui_demo: object|null ({zoom_target, cursor_path, clicks} for product-demo scenes)

parameters.name: vo_words_per_second
parameters.note: 120-150 wpm conversational; ~140 for narration; 160-170 only short/simple.

parameters.name: ui_demo_zoom
parameters.note: 1.5x if UI already readable; 3x is the cap (claustrophobic beyond).

parameters.name: ui_motion_duration
parameters.note: hover ~300, transition ~500; zoom 350-500 gentle / ~200 snappy; never linear.

parameters.name: signature_bezier_count
parameters.note: ease-out / ease-in / ease-in-out custom curves reused everywhere = motion equity.

parameters.name: ui_capture_min_fps
parameters.note: needed for clean cursor-path Bezier smoothing.

cognitive.name: Multimedia
cognitive.rule: Words + pictures beat words alone; never narrate over a blank/text-only frame.

cognitive.name: Coherence
cognitive.rule: Cut anything not serving the goal (decorative stings, gratuitous b-roll).

cognitive.name: Signaling
cognitive.rule: Cue the ONE element being discussed now (highlight/scale/motion).

cognitive.name: Redundancy
cognitive.rule: Narration + identical full on-screen text LOWERS retention; reserve text for short labels.

cognitive.name: Spatial/Temporal contiguity
cognitive.rule: Labels touch the thing; show the visual the moment the VO names it.

cognitive.name: Segmenting
cognitive.rule: Discrete beats with micro-pauses, learner-paced; not one unbroken rush.

cognitive.name: Modality
cognitive.rule: Narrate complex visuals (audio) rather than piling text on animation.

cognitive.name: Voice/Personalization
cognitive.rule: Conversational + human-sounding voice beats formal/robotic (d~0.78; modern TTS narrows it).

cognitive.name: Cognitive Load Theory
cognitive.rule: Working memory ~4 chunks; cut extraneous load so intrinsic load fits.

psychology.name: Front-load value
psychology.rule: Get to the point within ~10s; halves early viewership loss.

psychology.name: Curiosity gap / open loop
psychology.rule: Pose the question/promise up front, resolve at the payoff (Loewenstein, Zeigarnik). Keep the gap small/manageable.

pacing.name: Variable pacing
pacing.rule: Slow on comprehension beats (read/understand), fast on mechanical (cursor/transition); cut to BPM; breathers between dense beats.

motion.name: Disney 12 -> UI/MG
motion.rule: Slow-in/out (never linear), anticipation, staging, follow-through=stagger, arcs, squash/stretch, secondary action.

motion.name: Motion congruence (HARD law)
motion.rule: Kinematics must match meaning; bigger/heavier => slower; wrong motion reads as different meaning.

motion.name: Match cut
motion.rule: Carry one meaningful element across the cut (graphic match / match on action / color match / sound bridge).

motion.name: Kinetic typography
motion.rule: Settle fast then hold readable >=0.5s; hierarchy via sequence; one kinetic moment per section; never break a word; fit title-safe.

motion.name: Generate, never select
motion.rule: Compose form from tokens (stagger x order x easing) bounded by legibility laws; no fixed component library / template menu.

color.name: Semantic color fixed
color.rule: green=good/gain, red=bad/loss, amber=warning, blue=info; follow the data's meaning, never mood.

color.name: Mood via sat/bright/temp
color.rule: Mood = saturation + brightness + temperature, NOT hue; brand hue stays sovereign (Valdez & Mehrabian 1994).

color.name: Legibility floor
color.rule: WCAG 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large; on low-contrast footage escalate flip->shadow->stroke->scrim. Legibility beats mood.

sound.name: Music arc
sound.rule: Build tempo/layers toward the payoff; resolve at the end (real outro).

sound.name: SFX as punctuation
sound.rule: Use for emphasis/transitions/clicks/data-lands; sparingly + varied timbre; overuse (esp. repeated high-freq) = listener fatigue; silence on clean cuts/fades.

metrics.name: hold_rate
metrics.note: <25% after a strong hook = pacing problem.

contradictions.resolution: Platform-dependent: 9:16 vertical wins on social feeds; 16:9 horizontal wins on LinkedIn/B2B (beat 9:16 by 2-4x on a $140k test) and YouTube. Pick by platform+audience, do NOT hardcode 'vertical always'.
85% (Facebook) vs 92-95% (mobile/internal). Treat captions as mandatory regardless of which figure.
AI-blog sourced numbers are inconsistent (M). Only Wistia/Vidyard length-vs-retention curves are benchmark-grade. Calibrate per channel.
Classic d~0.78 favored human, but modern TTS (edge-tts) narrows it. Validate by ear; do not assume a robotic penalty.
